3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Evening descended on the capital as Lucian and I found ourselves alone in my office. I followed my chief strategist's eyes to the chessboard on the coffee table.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The sight of it reminded me of simpler times, of late-night strategy sessions turning into chess matches. We used to escape the political chaos into a world of rooks and bishops.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Our battles were both tense and friendly, a reflection of our long history together. Lucian had always proved a challenging opponent.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: His strategies, both on the chessboard and in politics, had the same unpredictable edge.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: A soft knock interrupted my reminiscing.

8.speaker: Livia Suno
8.text: "Long nights of strategy planning, and now a game of chess. You two never stop thinking, do you?"

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Livia came in with our usual coffee. She noticed the chessboard and smiled.

12.speaker: Lucian Galade
12.text: "I hope you remember that it's not always the king who holds the power. Sometimes, a well-placed pawn can change the game."

13.speaker: Player
13.text: "Livia, always a pleasure. Even more so when you bring coffee."

14.speaker: Player
14.text: "We might have to order dinner if this game takes as long as the ones we used to play."

15.speaker: Player
15.text: "What's your opinion on chess, Livia? Ever been tempted to learn?"

16.speaker: Livia Suno
16.text: "It's my job to keep the gears of this office turning, Mr. President."

17.speaker: Livia Suno
17.text: "I'll keep the Maroon Palace chef on speed dial then."

18.speaker: Livia Suno
18.text: "I prefer whist, Mr. President. I'll leave the complex plotting to the professionals."

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: She turned and left the room. Lucian acknowledged her exit with a slight nod, his eyes still fixed on the board.

21.speaker: Player
21.text: "Isn't that the truth? I've used pawns for some of my best plays."

22.speaker: Player
22.text: "Neither of them hold any real power, Lucian. It's the player who controls them."

23.speaker: Player
23.text: "The power dynamics of a chess board can teach us a lot about politics, wouldn't you agree, Lucian?"

24.speaker: Lucian Galade
24.text: "On the other hand, sir, even the most strategic pawn move won't help if you overlook the other pieces."

25.speaker: Lucian Galade
25.text: "Of course, sir. But a wise player recognizes the value of every piece on the board."

26.speaker: Lucian Galade
26.text: "Absolutely. And playing chess with politicians will tell you more about their goals and plans than any speech."

27.speaker: Narrator
27.text: His dexterous maneuvering reflected the unseen orchestration that helped Petr and me ascend through the ranks.

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: As Lucian positioned the pieces on the chessboard, it stirred memories of our early days in the United Sordland Party.

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: As the final piece was set into position, the board transformed into a silent battlefield.

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "Shall we get this game underway, Lucian?"

32.speaker: Lucian Galade
32.text: "Indeed, President Rayne. A game of chess is exactly what we need."

33.speaker: Lucian Galade
33.text: "Ah, the impatience of a president. Very well, let's begin."

34.speaker: Lucian Galade
34.text: "Which color do you prefer? Black as usual or white this time?"

35.speaker: Player
35.text: "Black for me. I like the advantage of reacting."

36.speaker: Player
36.text: "Doesn't matter to me, Lucian. I can play either side."

37.speaker: Player
37.text: "I'll take white. The honor of the first move."

38.speaker: Lucian Galade
38.text: "A fine choice, befitting of your drive to lead. The first move is yours, sir."

39.speaker: Lucian Galade
39.text: "A strategist's choice. I'm not surprised. The board is yours to react to."

40.speaker: Lucian Galade
40.text: "If it doesn't matter, allow me the honor of the first move. I'll take white."

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: With the sides chosen, Lucian sat back, his fingers laced together in contemplation.

47.speaker: Player
47.text: "I always enjoy a good challenge, Lucian. The Xinan should keep us both on our toes."

48.speaker: Player
48.text: "Well, Lucian, they do say the Xinan Defense is the best form of attack."

49.speaker: Player
49.text: "I thought I'd mix things up a bit, Lucian. Let's see how well you handle the Xinan."

50.speaker: Player
50.text: "Reti? Let's throw in a bit of spice."

51.speaker: Player
51.text: "It's not always about the center, is it?

53.speaker: Lucian Galade
53.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. I look forward to seeing your next moves."

54.speaker: Lucian Galade
54.text: "It's a dance of strategy, Mr. Rayne. Let's hope we both brought our dancing shoes."

55.speaker: Lucian Galade
55.text: "That they do, Mr. President. Let's see if it holds true for us today."

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: And thus the game began. The opening decision was mine.

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: Lucian moved his knight from g1 to f3. Aiming for a Reti Opening.

63.speaker: Lucian Galade
63.text: "Ah, symmetry. An art form in itself."

64.speaker: Lucian Galade
64.text: "A solid move, Mr. Rayne. Maintaining control of the center is often key."

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: Lucian's next move was calculated and swift. The bishop glided from f1 to g2, preparing for a potential kingside castle and fortifying the pawn structure.

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: Lucian's response came in the form of a g2 to g3 pawn move, hinting at the decision to fianchetto his bishop.

67.speaker: Player
67.text: "It's still early to hide behind defenses, isn't it?"

68.speaker: Player
68.text: "Your bishop is on the move, I see."

70.speaker: Player
70.text: "An unconventional approach. I'm curious to see where this leads."

72.speaker: Player
72.text: "You're setting up your bishop, I see."

74.speaker: Lucian Galade
74.text: "One can never be too careful in the game of kings."

75.speaker: Lucian Galade
75.text: "Every piece has its role to play, Mr. President."

78.speaker: Lucian Galade
78.text: "You know what they say about variety."

81.speaker: Lucian Galade
81.text: "Ah, the Xinan. A bold choice, Mr. Rayne. This should be an interesting match."

82.speaker: Lucian Galade
82.text: "The King's Gambit, Mr. Rayne? A daring opening. It promises an exciting game."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "Risk is part of the game, Lucian. Let's see if it pays off."

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "The King's Gambit always guarantees an engaging game, Lucian. I'm looking forward to your response."

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "A little daring keeps the game interesting, Lucian. Let's see how you manage."

86.speaker: Lucian Galade
86.text: "Agreed, Mr. President. I'm eager to navigate the labyrinth you're constructing."

87.speaker: Lucian Galade
87.text: "Indeed, Mr. Rayne. May the best player prevail."

88.speaker: Lucian Galade
88.text: "So am I, Mr. President. Your move."

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: With this, the stage was set. The opening maneuvers had transformed into a mid-game battle of wits.

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: Each pawn push, every subtle repositioning, had been showing to Lucian's strategic prowess and my resilience.

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: The next move would prove crucial. Lucian's queen cut a path through the heart of the board, menacing my vulnerable kingside.

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: As Lucian departed, I thought about what he'd told me. I'd learned a thing or two, but the man was more of a mystery than ever.

94.speaker: Lucian Galade
94.text: "A sacrifice indeed, but one I'm willing to make."

95.speaker: Player
95.text: "That knight of yours... a daring sacrifice, Lucian."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "Your knight is mine, Lucian. A worthy sacrifice on your part, it seems."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "A bold decision, leaving your knight in such a precarious position, Lucian."

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: The stakes were sky-high. A bold pawn advance could release my rook's potential and threaten Lucian's knight. On the other hand, I could gamble with a Rummish Gambit, a risky play that could wrestle control of the center away from him.

102.speaker: Lucian Galade
102.text: "The high stakes and strategical intricacies of this game remind me of the trials I endured early in my career."

103.speaker: Lucian Galade
103.text: "A daring maneuver under fiery pressure. You're an adept tactician but this is far from over."

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: Lucian moved his rook from the corner, adding pressure on my exposed bishop.

105.speaker: Lucian Galade
105.text: "Ah, the Rummish Gambit. Pushing down the center. Bold, but risky."

107.speaker: Player
107.text: "Sometimes, one must gamble to win, Lucian."

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: He calmly slid his queen across the board, threatening my isolated pawn. His subtle smirk revealed he understood my gambit and was ready to counter.

114.speaker: Player
114.text: "Only through fire do we learn the nature of the material."

115.speaker: Player
115.text: "Isn't that what makes the game exciting?"

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: Lucian was in high spirits, his eyes gleaming with a rare look of contentment.

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: Lucian maintained a steady gaze, his face unreadable.

118.speaker: Lucian Galade
118.text: "Your defenses are commendable. But you are giving me too much space."

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: Lucian, undeterred by my fortress, slid his queen to a more advantageous square.

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: In response to my knight's threat, Lucian moved out the threat, creating a barrier between my knight and his king.

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "Fire is the test of gold, Lucian."

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "All the more room for your downfall."

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: The center was congested, a show of Lucian's unyielding style. His formation was formidable, his pieces interlocked in a matrix of support, each protecting the other while simultaneously projecting threats across the board.

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: It was my move and the game had entered its final stages. Lucian's queen was uncomfortably close, radiating danger. I had only a few paths before me.

139.speaker: Lucian Galade
139.text: "A daring choice, President. It seems the end is near."

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: Lucian's king stood vulnerable, but a risky move could leave my own king exposed. However, seizing the opportunity seemed worth the risk.

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: The game was on a knife's edge, the outcome far from certain. The board offered a potential for a draw if I played conservatively or an opportunity for a hail mary win if I dared to go all in.

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: The game was slipping from my grasp. I had two options - a risky knight sacrifice that could lead to a swift end, or to hunker down and hope for a draw.

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: If Lucian overlooked the threat I posed, victory would be mine. If he identified the trap, the game could stretch on, but the advantage would be mine.

144.speaker: Lucian Galade
144.text: "A cautious play, sir. You are forcing us into a drawn endgame."

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: If Lucian tried to attack aggressively now, the fortress I'd built around my king would be my saving grace, leading to a draw. If he chose to fortify his position as well, a drawn endgame would be inevitable.

146.speaker: Lucian Galade
146.text: "A bold sacrifice. Let's see how this plays out."

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: If Lucian fell into the trap, I might manage to draw. If he saw through it, my loss was imminent.

148.speaker: Lucian Galade
148.text: "You're on the defensive. The endgame is mine to command."

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: If Lucian made a mistake now, I could potentially salvage a draw. However, if he played his cards right, defeat was the only outcome I could see.

150.speaker: Lucian Galade
150.text: "Ah, looking for a draw, Mr. President? Interesting."

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: If Lucian fell into the repetition pattern, a draw would be secured. If he managed to evade and counter, the game could still be saved.

152.speaker: Lucian Galade
152.text: "Taking a gamble, are we, President Rayne? Let's see where this leads."

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: If Lucian fell for my bold play, a miraculous victory might be snatched from the jaws of defeat. However, if he played cautiously, my loss would be inevitable.

154.speaker: Lucian Galade
154.text: "Well played. But it's not over yet."

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: Despite Lucian's attempt to wriggle out, his king was trapped. My queen delivered the final blow, spelling a checkmate. The game was over, and I had won.

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: With both of us refusing to risk our positions, the game ended in a stalemate. Neither side had managed to achieve victory.

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: Lucian, caught in my trap, tried to navigate his king out of the danger zone.

159.speaker: Narrator
159.text: Lucian, sensing my defensive play, bolstered his own defenses.

160.speaker: Lucian Galade
160.text: "You're not the only one who can play this game."

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: The checks continued, neither of us giving ground. With the position repeating three times, the game was declared a draw due to the threefold repetition rule.

162.speaker: Lucian Galade
162.text: "I see your gamble, and I raise you a castle."

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: My daring gamble fell flat. Lucian's defense was unbreakable, and I had no more tricks up my sleeve. His queen swooped in for the final checkmate. The game was over, and Lucian had won.

164.speaker: Narrator
164.text: Lucian tried to maneuver his king away from the repeated checks.

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: Lucian chose not to take the bait, instead strengthening his defenses against my desperate gamble.

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: My bold move backfired. Lucian's pieces closed in, trapping my king. It was checkmate. The game was over, and Lucian had won.

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: His attack was ruthless. I couldn't withstand it. My king was cornered, and with a final, decisive move, Lucian declared checkmate. The game was over, and I had lost.

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: Lucian seized the opportunity, capturing my sacrificed knight and strengthening his position.

171.speaker: Narrator
171.text: Lucian decided to press his advantage, launching an aggressive attack on my defensive shell.

172.speaker: Player
172.text: "Your king is trapped, Lucian. The game is mine."

173.speaker: Player
173.text: "Checkmate, my friend. It was a well-fought battle."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "It seems the king is cornered, Lucian. Good game."

175.speaker: Player
175.text: "We've reached an impasse, Lucian. A draw it is."

176.speaker: Player
176.text: "A stalemate, then. Quite the battle, Lucian."

177.speaker: Player
177.text: "It looks like neither of us could secure the victory, Lucian."

178.speaker: Lucian Galade
178.text: "Indeed, Mr. Rayne. You've played well. Congratulations."

179.speaker: Lucian Galade
179.text: "I see no way out. Well done, Mr. President. You've earned this victory."

180.speaker: Lucian Galade
180.text: "It's your win, President Rayne. You've played an impressive game."

181.speaker: Lucian Galade
181.text: "Yes, Mr. Rayne. It's a fitting end to a well-fought game."

182.speaker: Lucian Galade
182.text: "A draw, indeed. Here is to our equally matched skills."

183.speaker: Lucian Galade
183.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. It's a stalemate. Good game."

184.speaker: Player
184.text: "We're at a stalemate, Lucian. It's a draw."

185.speaker: Player
185.text: "Neither victory nor defeat, Lucian. A draw it is."

186.speaker: Player
186.text: "A draw, then. You've managed to evade my checks, Lucian."

187.speaker: Lucian Galade
187.text: "Yes, President Rayne. It was a challenging game, leading us to a draw."

188.speaker: Lucian Galade
188.text: "Neither of us could deliver the final blow. A draw it is, Mr. President."

189.speaker: Lucian Galade
189.text: "It's a deadlock, Mr. President. A game well played."

190.speaker: Player
190.text: "My gamble didn't pay off, Lucian. You've won."

191.speaker: Player
191.text: "You've defended well, Lucian. It's your win."

192.speaker: Player
192.text: "You've seen through my gamble, Lucian. Well played."

193.speaker: Lucian Galade
193.text: "Your bold move made for an interesting endgame, President Rayne. Good game."

194.speaker: Lucian Galade
194.text: "Your gamble was a risky one, President Rayne. In this case, I prevailed."

195.speaker: Lucian Galade
195.text: "You played daringly, Mr. President. But this time, the game is mine."

196.speaker: Player
196.text: "You've trapped my king, Lucian. The game is yours."

197.speaker: Player
197.text: "Your strategy was superior, Lucian. I admit defeat."

199.speaker: Lucian Galade
199.text: "Thank you, Mr. President. You've put up quite a fight."

200.speaker: Lucian Galade
200.text: "You played well, Mr. President. Better luck next time."

201.speaker: Lucian Galade
201.text: "The game was tough, Mr. President. Your defeat was not easily won."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "My king is cornered, Lucian. Well done."

203.speaker: Player
203.text: "You've broken through my defenses, Lucian. It's your win."

204.speaker: Player
204.text: "Your attack was relentless, Lucian. I concede."

205.speaker: Lucian Galade
205.text: "Your defenses were tough to crack, President Rayne. Good game."

206.speaker: Lucian Galade
206.text: "Victory wasn't easy, Mr. President. You made me work for it."

207.speaker: Lucian Galade
207.text: "Your game was strong, Mr. President. But in the end, I prevailed."

212.speaker: Lucian Galade
212.text: "Ah, a swift strike at the heart, Mr. President. The game grows more interesting."

213.speaker: Lucian Galade
213.text: "Clever, President Rayne. But did you consider all the consequences?"

214.speaker: Narrator
214.text: Lucian had made a bold move, pushing his pawn forward and forcing my bishop into a vulnerable position.

215.speaker: Narrator
215.text: While the urge to secure my threatened bishop was strong, an enticing opportunity also lay before me: a potential double attack on Lucian's king and rook.

220.speaker: Lucian Galade
220.text: "Maybe another match another time. If fate allows."

221.speaker: Lucian Galade
221.text: "Time well spent. We learn less from victories though."

222.speaker: Narrator
222.text: Lucian and I slowly began to dismantle the chessboard, each piece carefully placed back into its protective casing.

223.speaker: Narrator
223.text: Lucian responded to my King's Gambit with a cautious but smart move, advancing his knight to f6.

224.speaker: Narrator
224.text: As a response to my Xinan Defense, Lucian surprised me by opting for the Open Xinan, advancing his pawn to d4.

225.speaker: Narrator
225.text: This was the Falkbeer Counter Gambit, directly attacking my e4 pawn while leaving my f4 pawn hanging.

226.speaker: Player
226.text: "Your move shows your experience, Lucian. This game is shaping up to be quite a match."

227.speaker: Player
227.text: "I see you aren't one to back down from a challenge, Lucian. Very well."

228.speaker: Player
228.text: "A Falkbeer Counter Gambit, Lucian? You certainly know how to keep things interesting."

230.speaker: Lucian Galade
230.text: "One does try, Mr. Rayne. It's your move."

231.speaker: Lucian Galade
231.text: "I wouldn't expect anything less from you, Mr. President."

232.speaker: Lucian Galade
232.text: "It wouldn't be much of a game if I did, now would it, Mr. Rayne?"

235.speaker: Narrator
235.text: He was pushing for control of the center early, looking to turn the game into a tactical melee.

236.speaker: Player
236.text: "Bold strategy, Lucian. It seems we're in for a battle of tactics."

237.speaker: Player
237.text: "I see you're trying to seize the center early, Lucian. That's an aggressive play."

238.speaker: Player
238.text: "The Open Xinan, Lucian? You're certainly not shy about your intentions."

240.speaker: Lucian Galade
240.text: "Why hide, Mr. Rayne? Chess is a game of strategy and confrontation."

241.speaker: Lucian Galade
241.text: "That's the essence of chess, Mr. President."

242.speaker: Lucian Galade
242.text: "Aggression can be a key to victory, Mr. Rayne."

257.speaker: Narrator
257.text: Lucian's eyes bore a far-off look. Perhaps he was replaying the match within his mind.

258.speaker: Narrator
258.text: He picked up a knight and turned it over in his hand thoughtfully.

259.speaker: Narrator
259.text: The chess match seemed to have left him thoughtful, his mind perhaps mulling over the moves he could have made.

260.speaker: Lucian Galade
260.text: "This game always reminds me of the delicate balance we had to strike in the days of the old Kingdom."

261.speaker: Lucian Galade
261.text: "A difficult game, chess. The constant threats and counter-threats take me back to some similarly challenging times."

262.speaker: Lucian Galade
262.text: "Although the situation there was rarely as black and white."

263.speaker: Lucian Galade
263.text: "It was not always a simple task."

264.speaker: Player
264.text: "You certainly know how to keep things interesting, Lucian. Your past seems to be a well-guarded secret."

265.speaker: Player
265.text: "Strategical intricacies, eh? Sounds like you've got some interesting stories about that career. Care to share one?"

266.speaker: Player
266.text: "Tell me more. Did chess play a part in your youth?"

267.speaker: Player
267.text: "Threats and counter-threats... your past seems a lot more interesting than mine."

268.speaker: Player
268.text: "Was there a particular challenge that still resonates?"

269.speaker: Player
269.text: "Sounds like you've had quite the complicated past."

270.speaker: Player
270.text: "This balance you speak of, Lucian, it seems to hint at some intriguing aspects of your past."

271.speaker: Player
271.text: "I can't help but wonder what kind of situations you had to navigate, Lucian."

272.speaker: Player
272.text: "Balance in the days of the old Kingdom? Lucian, have you been holding back some history from me?"

273.speaker: Lucian Galade
273.text: "In a way, chess prepared me for some of the challenges I faced."

274.speaker: Lucian Galade
274.text: "I was involved in some complex situations, where every move could drastically alter the landscape."

275.speaker: Lucian Galade
275.text: "Some things from those days are better left unsaid. I will say there was a certain...duality to those times."

276.speaker: Lucian Galade
276.text: "Chess is not the only game where one has to maintain a balance."

277.speaker: Lucian Galade
277.text: "We all have our pasts, Mr. President."

278.speaker: Lucian Galade
278.text: "Mine happened to involve many moves and counter-moves, each with its own consequences."

279.speaker: Player
279.text: "Every move altering the landscape? Your early career must have been quite eventful."

280.speaker: Player
280.text: "Complex situations, you say? Sounds like you've dealt with a lot of tough decisions."

281.speaker: Player
281.text: "Were these consequences a part of the old Kingdom's final years, Lucian?"

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "Moves and counter-moves? So you've seen your share of conflict."

284.speaker: Player
284.text: "It sounds like you were in the thick of it."

285.speaker: Lucian Galade
285.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. My past isn't without its share of shadows. There was a time when I served in a capacity that wasn't so... straightforward."

286.speaker: Narrator
286.text: Lucian's gaze dropped to his empty glass as he fell into a moment of quiet introspection.

287.speaker: Lucian Galade
287.text: "Mr. President, the old Kingdom was a cauldron of shifting alliances and loyalties."

288.speaker: Narrator
288.text: Lucian shut the chess box with a soft click. He seemed unwilling to say more.

289.speaker: Lucian Galade
289.text: "Yes, Mr. President, those were trying times for Sordland. And like many others, I was caught in the crossfire of those tumultuous years."

290.speaker: Narrator
290.text: A shadow seemed to pass over Lucian's eyes, a hint of the turmoil that still lingered in his memory.

291.speaker: Lucian Galade
291.text: "I can tell you that there were instances where I found myself in the midst of... let's call it, intelligence work."

292.speaker: Lucian Galade
292.text: "I danced on a knife-edge, every step carrying deep consequences."

293.speaker: Player
293.text: "You're beginning to intrigue me, Lucian. What are you not telling me?"

294.speaker: Player
294.text: "Can you tell me more about this... different capacity you served in?"

295.speaker: Player
295.text: "I certainly don't wish to delve into matters that might unsettle you."

296.speaker: Lucian Galade
296.text: "I've reconciled with my past, sir. I don't shy away from sharing aspects of it with those I trust."

297.speaker: Lucian Galade
297.text: "It was a complex dance, rife with deception and shadows."

298.speaker: Lucian Galade
298.text: "Let's just say I was one of many who had to navigate those treacherous waters."

299.speaker: Player
299.text: "We've known each other for years, and that's all I get?"

300.speaker: Player
300.text: "Treacherous waters... were you a naval officer?"

301.speaker: Player
301.text: "I certainly don't wish to delve into matters that might unsettle you."

302.speaker: Player
302.text: "What sort of conflicts are we talking about?"

303.speaker: Player
303.text: "Caught in the crossfire... were you in the military?"

304.speaker: Lucian Galade
304.text: "It is not my intent to withhold information from you. But I believe we should focus on the future of Sordland, and leave its history where it belongs."

305.speaker: Lucian Galade
305.text: "It's a discussion for another day, Mr. President. Suffice to say, it was a time when Sordland was a battleground of older ideals and ambitions."

306.speaker: Lucian Galade
306.text: "My role? Let's just say I was one of the pieces on the board."

307.speaker: Lucian Galade
307.text: "I've reconciled with my past and set it aside."

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "So you were a spy? Sounds fascinating."

309.speaker: Player
309.text: "Cut the metaphors, Lucian. I want details."

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "You were involved in intelligence work, Lucian? That's certainly an unexpected revelation."

311.speaker: Lucian Galade
311.text: "It's true, sir. During the late Kingdom era, I found myself part of King Egmund's intelligence service."

312.speaker: Lucian Galade
312.text: "In a manner many would find... objectionable."

313.speaker: Lucian Galade
313.text: "There's much I still cannot say. But I carried out some unconventional assignments for King Egmund."

314.speaker: Lucian Galade
314.text: "I served in a capacity that often demanded... morally challenging choices."

315.speaker: Lucian Galade
315.text: "'Spy' is a simplistic term, Mr. President. My past roles were, let's say, less than conventional."

316.speaker: Lucian Galade
316.text: "I served for the national interests of King Egmund."

317.speaker: Lucian Galade
317.text: "Much as I'd love to elaborate, I must take my leave. Thank you for the delightful match."

318.speaker: Lucian Galade
318.text: "On that note, it's time for me to depart. I thoroughly enjoyed our match tonight, Mr. President."

319.speaker: Player
319.text: "It's always a pleasure to witness your strategic prowess."

320.speaker: Player
320.text: "Delightful for you, maybe. I demand a rematch."

321.speaker: Player
321.text: "Thank you, Lucian. The match was indeed captivating."

323.speaker: Player
323.text: "As did I. The game was as enlightening as it was entertaining."

324.speaker: Player
324.text: "Indeed, the game was a great pleasure, Lucian. Safe travels home."

325.speaker: Lucian Galade
325.text: "I hope to play again soon. Though I cannot promise the outcome will be any different for you."

326.speaker: Lucian Galade
326.text: "Win or lose, there's always something to be learned from a round of chess."

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: As Lucian exited the room, the memories of our game lingered, as did the enigmatic aura of the man himself.

337.speaker: Narrator
337.text: A few minutes passed and a few more actions were made on the board.
